properties.name: Someone can read what reflow2 is on the open web, without cloning it or installing anything
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, sequenced explicitly AFTER the next release: *"post release, i'd like to do something like this for: To show your repository's HTML files on a live web page like username.github.io, use GitHub Pages."*

WHAT IS ASKED FOR, stated only as far as he stated it: reflow2's repository publishes a live web page on GitHub Pages, reachable at a public URL, so a reader meets the project without cloning the repo, installing the binary, or running an agent. Today every description of reflow2 lives in files you must already have checked out.

HE SUPPLIED A MECHANISM SKETCH AND IT IS NOT TAKEN AS SETTLED, because he prefaced it with "something like this": `index.html` at the repository root, Pages configured to deploy from a branch (`main`, folder `/root`). ⚠️ THE ROOT PLACEMENT IS THE PART TO RE-EXAMINE RATHER THAN IMPLEMENT — this repository's root is a Rust workspace (`Cargo.toml`, `crates/`), and GitHub Pages also serves from `/docs` or from an Actions deploy, both of which keep generated HTML out of the build root. Which mechanism is right is a decision, not a transcription.

📌 ALREADY PRESENT AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT: `docs/loop-dag.html` is the repo's one existing HTML page, and `tools/render_views.py` already renders design viewpoints as pure projections with a CONFESSIONS list for anything the graph cannot supply.

⚠️ WHAT THE PAGE SHOWS IS NOT STATED AND IS NOT INFERRED HERE. That question is `dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page`, and it is the one that decides how much work this is.

ACCEPTED 2026-09-28: Anthony confirmed the wording, including the extension below ("yes, accept wording on the three requirements").

EXTENDED 2026-09-28 on Anthony's word (kept as intent from dec:idea-the-repo-front-door-is-minimal-and-the-documentation-is-a-small-site). The page becomes reflow2's documentation, not only a showcase:
· The documentation moves out of docs/ into a few clean pages on the site (sligara7.github.io/reflow2), laid out like flo2.io.
· The pages are GENERATED from reflow2's own design, as dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page requires (reaffirmed the same day), not hand-written.
· The repository's front door is a minimal README: what reflow2 is, how to install it, and a link to the site. GitHub renders no index.html on a repository page, so a README is the one front door a visitor there sees.
· Where Pages serves from (/docs, a gh-pages branch, or an Actions deploy) stays to be chosen, as the 2026-08-14 text already said, because the root is a Rust workspace.
The docs/ files registered as Artifacts retire on the record as their content moves into the design the site renders. Nothing is deleted without a home.
